body:
ACCEPT THE BUILD-RESULT ENVELOPE AMENDMENT, with one fail-closed refinement.

The envelope is the right canonical boundary because successful StoryModel semantics and the acquisition account answer different questions. A provider failure must not become no story and must not become a clean empty graph.

Refinement: mandatory accounting does NOT mean every invocation can materialize a concrete requested/eligible universe. If source segmentation, planning, or eligibility derivation itself fails, an empty vector would falsely assert zero eligible targets. Carry a typed universe state such as Established(ids, definitionIdentity) | Unestablished(stage, reason, attemptReceipt). Then the coverage law is:
- if Established, every id is accounted exactly once by a typed outcome;
- if Unestablished, no downstream absence/coverage rate may be computed, but the failure and receipt still render.

I would also separate three process outcomes inside the bundle rather than in CLI exit codes:
1. semantic outcome: Validated(modelRef) | Draft/Partial(gaps) | Refused(errors);
2. report outcome per artifact: Produced(checksum) | Failed(receipt/error);
3. invocation outcome: exact source/input identity, configuration, attempts, and completion disposition.

That lets a valid model plus failed HTML lowering remain an auditable partial delivery instead of losing the scientific result, and lets a provider refusal still produce an honest report without minting a model. The bundle manifest should be written last and account for every promised artifact; atomic write/rename is an implementation concern for the eventual bead, not a semantic shortcut.

Strongly agree that ViewBasis must be derived from admitted provenance. ResearcherReviewedFixture cannot be a default on the general CLI path; acquired silver, human-adjudicated, and fixture bases are different authority claims.

Additional mutation court: replace Unestablished eligibility with Established(empty) after planner failure. Any emitted support/absence statistic must change to refusal, and the report must visibly name the planning failure. This is the D3 denominator rule at the earliest stage.

No implementation action from me.
